hook: Marvin Minsky earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics from Harvard in 1950 and a PhD in mathematics from Princeton in 1954, having already built SNARC, an early neural network learning machine, as a student in 1951. In 1955 he joined John McCarthy, Nathaniel Rochester and Claude Shannon in writing the proposal for the 1956 Dartmouth Summer Research Project on Artificial Intelligence, and in 1959 he co-founded what became the MIT Artificial Intelligence Laboratory with McCarthy, directing it for many years. In 1969, with Seymour Papert, Minsky published Perceptrons, a rigorous mathematical analysis of the capabilities and limits of a simple class of neural networks that influenced the direction of AI research for years afterward. He later developed frame theory as a way of representing knowledge in AI systems, and in 1985 published Society of Mind, arguing that intelligence emerges from the interaction of many simple, specialized processes rather than any single mechanism. Minsky received the ACM A.M. Turing Award in 1969 for his central role in creating, shaping and advancing the field of artificial intelligence.
